chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa transmitted it from Samaan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, when is the time for the prayer?' He turned his head right and left, as if looking for something. When I saw that, I took a stick and said, 'Are you looking for this?' He said, 'Yes.' He took the stick and placed it in front of the sun, then said, 'When the sun rises, the shadow is long, then it continues to decrease until the sun declines (reaches its zenith). When it declines, the shadow increases. When you perceive the increase, pray Dhuhr. Then delay for the length of a cubit and pray Asr.'
ai.seo_question: How to determine the exact time for Dhuhr and Asr prayers using the sun's shadow?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the practical application of shadow observation to distinguish between Dhuhr and Asr, using a stick to visualize the sun's position. This method highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise astronomical markers for prayer times, specifically defining the start of Asr as the moment the shadow equals the length of an object (excluding the shadow at zenith). The instruction to delay Asr slightly after its onset reflects the preference for *istihbab* (recommended delay) to ensure the time has fully entered, aligning with juristic principles of caution in worship.
